title: Standing for 2+ hours is not for the faint of heart, but if your legs...
transcript: Have you ever watched a Broadway or off Broadway show from on stage? I just got to have that experience at Jesus Christ Superstar in London's West End, and it was honestly a lot cooler than I thought it was gonna be. For the show, tickets were £25 and you would stand in one of three different cages. Now, which cage you ended up in was random, and since you had to leave the stage during intermission, many people ended up in different cages. For Act 1 and 2, I, by chance, ended up in the stage right cage of both acts. And I definitely think these side cages are a better view than this back cage. While most of the show is played to the audience, so you do end up seeing a lot of backs, I did find that these actors are really good at cheating out, so most of the time you could see at least a side profile, so it ended up actually being a pretty decent view. While there aren't really any instances of direct interaction with the cast members, they do make a ton of eye contact with you, which really adds to the sense that you are a part of this group. One of my favourite things in theatre is seeing little moments between ensemble members just connect in some way, whether that's direct eye contact or smiling at one another. And I was on stage being like, oh, my god, I'm now having Those moments, and that was just so cool to me. And also because you're so close to the wings, like, you could see people backstage. You might hear some backstage whispers or see someone getting prepped to go on for their entrance. I got to see, at one point, Jesus comes off stage right before Gethsemane, does this little vocal warm up into a box, and then goes right back out on stage to sing his big song. And I just loved being able to see all of these behind the scenes moments. Like don't get me wrong, this is not the optimal way to view this show, but it is certainly the coolest. And for only £25, like, you can't beat it.
